set.approach: The Temple (Kangaroo Temple, on Kangaroo Ridge) is reached from the large pullout at the hairpin turns on SR-20 just east of Washington Pass — the same parking area used for the neighboring Hairpin Crags/Spire Gully climbs. From the pullout, a climber's trail heads south across a boulder field, through forest and more talus (faint, intermittently cairned) up to Kangaroo Pass, about 1 hour. From the pass, an intermittent trail traverses to a gully between Kangaroo Temple and Little Finger; ascending or descending that gully reaches the base of the North Face, Northwest Face, or Southwest Face routes, roughly another hour. Total trailhead-to-summit time runs about 7-8 hours round trip. IMPORTANT — this route shares the approach to Kangaroo Pass with Temple's North/Northwest Face routes but finishes differently: rather than climbing toward the notch, drop some elevation below the pass and traverse across to the base of the South Face, roughly 2-4 hours from the car in all. The face isn't visible from the highway.

findings.claim: approach first describes the Kangaroo Pass approach, then says the South Face route hikes southeast along the creek and 'never crosses Kangaroo Pass'
findings.evidence: The route page for this climb (Kangaroo Temple South Face, III 5.8, Marts/Marts/McPherson 1965) gives the approach as: park at the hairpin, hike southeast to Kangaroo Pass, then drop some elevation and traverse to the South Face, 2-4 hours. The area page likewise says to go DOWN from the Temple–Little Finger gully for the southwest-side route. The 'southeast, right side of the creek/timber' hike in the stored clause is the approach TO Kangaroo Pass (the valley southeast of the hairpin), not an alternative that avoids it. Only the contradictory closing clause was replaced; 'Longer and steeper' dropped because it described the non-existent separate approach, replaced by the sourced 2-4 hr total. Side note: the route page gives 8 pitches / 800 ft; stored is 7 pitches / 244 m, and other descriptions say seven pitches, so no classification change proposed.

set.fa: Original aid line: Jim Langdon and Mead Hargis, 1969. First free ascent: Blake Herrington and Max Tepfer, 2015

findings.claim: fa lists only the 1969 aid line; the free variation was climbed in 2015 by Herrington and Tepfer
findings.evidence: Blake Herrington and Max Tepfer freed the original 1969 Langdon–Hargis (5.8 A4) route on Supercave/M&M Wall over three days in summer 2015, adding 3 bolts with Langdon's permission. The stored overview already says so; fa now carries it as a plain ascent credit (climbers credited as ascensionists, not as a source).

set.overview: The hardest documented route on Prusik Peak: a 5.14a big-wall-style testpiece up the southwest face headwall, first aided by Fitz Cahall and freed by Adrian Vanoni.

findings.claim: overview calls it a 'south face' route; it is on the southwest face
findings.evidence: The AAJ free-ascent report and the Climbing news report both place the route on Prusik Peak's southwest face. One-word fix: 'south face headwall' -> 'southwest face headwall'.

findings.claim: a report saw no bolt at the top of the crux pitch — check any bolt claim in anchor/beta prose
findings.evidence: beta, overview and descent_text make no bolt claim for the top of P6. pitch_detail P6 says 'single bolt backed up with a small cam', which matches the route page ('single-bolt belay backed up with purple or green cam') and the AAJ description of anchoring by bolts plus gear. One contrary observation does not outweigh two sources; nothing changed (pitch_detail is outside this batch anyway).

Sources count 7 pitches / 600 ft, but the 7th is the West Ridge scramble to the summit; six roped pitches is a defensible count and the stored table already has a separate scramble row. No classification change proposed; a reviewer may prefer 7 to match published counts.

wa_davis_holland_route.skip_reason: no rappels or descent_text is stored for this route, so there is no claim to correct; adding a descent would be new material outside this batch

findings.claim: descent: the P3 anchor cannot be rappelled to the ground with one 60 m rope; rap to a hanging anchor, then more raps trending left
findings.evidence: Consistent with sources (from the P3 belay: one double-rope rap to the ground, or a couple of 20-30 m raps trending climber's left via sport-wall anchors), but rappels and descent_text are both null, so nothing stored contradicts it. pitch_detail P3 only says 'most parties rappel', which is true. Suggest a future enrichment add a descent. Also: fa lacks the year; sources give 1965 for Dan Davis and John Holland (not changed; not the finding).
The route page grades it 5.10d with the 10d crux on P2; the FA-era trip report is titled 5.10d; the stored pitch_detail already marks P2 as the 5.10d crux.

grade.evidence: Route page and FA-era report both give 5.10d; stored pitch_detail P2 crux is 5.10d. '5.10+' is a looser rendering of the same grade.

wa_south_spur.skip_reason: report only — grade sources disagree; climbing_route not to be edited

findings.claim: grade '4th' — recent reports call the summit ridge Class 3
findings.evidence: The route listing gives South Spur as 4th class PG13; several trip reports describe the south ridge crest as an exposed Class 3 scramble (one calls the descent 'class 2+'). Stored '4th' is the published catalog grade and trip-report grades vary with snow and line, so no classification change proposed.

findings.claim: climbing_route step 3 'on the order of a hundred feet' is unconfirmed
findings.evidence: No source found giving a length for the summit ridge scramble; reports only call it 'short'. Reported only, not edited, per instructions.

wa_little_sister_southeast_ridge.skip_reason: report only — area-level elevation, not in this batch

findings.evidence: Twin Sisters range listings give Little Sister as 6,600 ft (2,012 m); no route prose column on this route states the elevation. The area-level value should be checked against the USGS map/DEM by a human.

wa_davis_peak_nc_north_face.skip_reason: sources disagree on the FA year; the winter date is not clearly contradicted

findings.claim: fa says July 1974 or 1976; a peak page gives 1972 for Kloke and Simon
findings.evidence: The peak page gives 1972; a 1988 AAJ report refers to 'the 1974 Kloke-Simon route'; the stored text already records 1974/1976. Three years across sources, so they do not clearly agree and fa is left as is. A reviewer could widen it to 'recorded variously as 1972, 1974 or 1976'.
The trip report is titled 3/12/2005 (plausibly the start of a multi-day push); its body would not load to confirm the summit-ridge day. Not changed.
